correctness.rationale: Analytically: uniqueness and O(d-1) invariance restrict the maximal ellipsoid to E(a,b,s). Exact cap and side support containment is s>=b,s+b<=1,ks+sqrt(a^2+k^2b^2)<=1. At optimum s=b (k>0); maximizing b(1-2kb)^((d-1)/2) on (0,1/2] has the single critical point 1/[(d+1)k], yielding the two exact regimes. Cylinder k=0 checked separately. For reflection, the minimum of each lateral linear functional is -1 at the base, giving exact cap and side constraints; their optimization proves global sigma=1/(2-r) and unique center, and substitution of b proves the three regimes and all endpoint coincidences. Supplementary fraction arithmetic and boundary sampling in verify.py do not establish infinite-dimensional quantification by themselves.

value.rationale: A natural continuum from a cone to a cylinder has a sharp structural event where the John ellipsoid first contacts the upper cap at r=(d-1)/(d+1). Within an additional nontrivial radius interval the reflection coefficient of its John center is exactly flat d/(d+2) while the center itself moves. The full classification and unique Minkowski center produce a concrete, theoretically motivated comparison between two distinct canonical notions of center.
